q: 1. A temporary rigid structure having platforms to enable masons to work at different stages of a building, is known as
explain: Scaffolding is a temporary structure used to support a work crew and materials to aid in the construction, maintenance, and repair of buildings.

q: 2. The brick which is cut such that at one end half the width is maintained and at the other end full width is maintained is called ...........
explain: A beveled closer has one full-length stretcher face, but the width at one end is cut to be half the width of the brick.

q: 3. A brick or stone put in position in the masonry such that its length is parallel to the face of the wall is known as ...........
explain: A stretcher is a brick laid with its longest side (length) parallel to the face of the wall.

q: 4. Cavity wall
options: prevent dampness from entering the building
have lesser dead load for given wall thickness
provide better insulation for heat & sound
explain: Cavity walls are multifunctional: they block capillary moisture, reduce building weight, and improve the indoor climate through air-gap insulation.

q: 5. The bricks arranged projecting in alternate courses for the purpose of bonding future masonry work is called ...........
explain: Toothing is the process of leaving bricks projecting from a wall so that another wall can be bonded into it later.

q: 6. The portion of brick obtained by cutting a brick lengthwise into two directions is known as
explain: A queen closer is made by cutting a brick lengthwise into two equal halves, often used next to a quoin header.

q: 7. A projected ornamental course near the top of the wall or near the junction of the wall and ceiling is known as ...
explain: A cornice is a decorative horizontal molding that crowns a building or furniture element, typically found at the top of a wall.

q: 8. The covering on the exposed top of a wall is called ...........
explain: Coping is a protective cap or cover (usually stone or brick) on the top of a wall to shed water and prevent moisture from entering the wall.

q: 9. A brick which has one or two rounded edges and used to obtain rounded corners in the wall is called .......
explain: A bull nose brick is manufactured with one or more rounded edges, used for aesthetics or to prevent sharp corners on walls.

q: 10. The English bond in which the corners of the wall are strengthened by starting every stretcher course with a three fourth bat at the quoin and a header is placed next to the three fourth bat at the quoin in alternate stretcher course is called ..........
explain: Dutch bond is a variation of English bond that uses a specific arrangement of bats and headers at the quoin to improve appearance and strength.

q: 11. When two walls separated by a small gap, are connected together by metal pins, it is called .......
explain: A cavity wall consists of two leaves of masonry separated by an air space (cavity) and connected by metal wall ties.

q: 12. A temporary rigid structure having platform to enable masons to work at different stages of a building is known as
explain: Scaffolding is the temporary framework used to support workers and materials during the construction or repair of a building.

q: 13. The bearing of the lintel should be
explain: The minimum bearing (overlap on the wall) for a lintel is usually 10 cm, the height of the lintel, or 1/12th of the span—whichever is greatest.

q: 14. If the center of the arch lies on the springing line, it is ..........
explain: A semi-circular arch has its center exactly on the line connecting the two springing points.

q: 15. An arch in the form of a perfect circle used for circular windows is called ..........
explain: A bull's eye arch is a complete 360-degree circular arch often used for aesthetic ventilation or windows.

q: 16. The wall constructed along the slopes to protect the slopes of cutting from the adverse effect of atmosphere are called as
explain: Breast walls are designed specifically to prevent the weathering or 'slipping' of natural soil slopes, whereas retaining walls are meant to resist the active earth pressure of a backfill.

q: 17. A wall constructed to withstand the pressure of an earth filling is known as ..........
explain: Retaining walls are designed to resist the lateral pressure of soil or earth when there is a change in ground elevation.

q: 18. The lower half of the arch between the crown and the skewback is known as
explain: The haunch is the middle portion of the arch between the crown (top) and the springing (base).

q: 19. Expansion joints in masonry walls are provided if length exceeds ..........
explain: According to standard practice, expansion joints in long masonry walls are provided when the length exceeds 40 meters.

q: 20. The least thickness of a stone masonry wall is ..........
explain: Due to the irregular size of stones, the minimum practical thickness for a stone masonry wall is generally 350 mm.

q: 21. A temporary rigid structure having platforms raised up as the building increases in height, is called ..........
explain: Scaffolding is a temporary framework used to provide a safe working platform for laborers and materials during construction or repair.

q: 22. The brick laid with its length perpendicular to the face of the wall is called a ..........
explain: A header is a brick laid so that only its end (the smaller face) is visible on the surface of the wall.

q: 23. A system of providing temporary support to the party walls of two buildings when the intermediate building is to be pulled down and built, is called ..........
explain: Flying shores (horizontal shores) support two parallel walls across an open space without touching the ground.

q: 24. Coping is defined as a ..........
options: horizontal course of masonry projecting from the face of the wall
horizontal moulded projection near the top of a building
covering placed on the exposed top of an external wall
triangular shaped portion of masonry at the end of a sloped roof
explain: Coping is a protective cap (usually stone or concrete) placed on top of a wall to shed water and prevent moisture from entering the masonry.

q: 25. Hearting is the portion of a ..........
options: brick cut in such a manner that its one long face remains uncut
explain: In thick walls, hearting is the interior portion of the wall between the exterior facing and the interior backing.

q: 26. In stretching bond ..........
options: all the bricks are laid as headers
all the bricks are laid as stretchers
the arrangement of bricks is similar to English bond
the bonding bricks are laid at any angle other than zero or ninety degrees
explain: Stretching bond consists entirely of stretchers and is used primarily for half-brick thick partition walls.

q: 27. A stretcher bond is usually used for ..........
explain: Since all bricks are laid lengthwise, a stretcher bond cannot provide a transverse bond, limiting it to half-brick (10cm) walls.

q: 28. A retaining wall may be built in ...........
explain: Retaining walls are designed to resist lateral earth pressure and can be constructed using various materials like dry stone (gravity), masonry, or reinforced/plain concrete depending on height and site conditions.

q: 29. Plain brick type of partition wall is constructed by ..........
options: laying bricks as stretchers in cement mortar
laying bricks as headers in cement mortar
reinforcing the brick wall with iron straps
brick work built within a frame-work of wooden members
explain: Plain brick partitions are typically half-brick thick (10 cm), achieved by laying bricks in the stretcher course.

q: 30. Brick noggin type of partition wall is constructed by ..........
options: laying bricks as stretchers in cement mortar
laying bricks as headers in cement mortar
reinforcing the brick wall with iron straps
brick work built within a frame-work of wooden members
explain: Brick nogging consists of a wooden framework (studs and noggins) filled with brickwork, used for stability and speed of construction.

q: 31. The sill in a wooden partition wall is the .......... wooden member.
explain: The sill is the lowest horizontal member of a frame that rests on the floor.

q: 32. The wedge shaped unit (voussoir) placed at the crown of an arch, is called ..........
explain: The keystone is the central wedge-shaped stone at the summit of an arch, locking the whole together.

q: 33. To construct a 10 cm thick partition wall, preferred bond will be ..........
explain: A 10 cm wall is exactly the width of a single brick's length (stretcher side), hence stretcher bond is used.

q: 34. Frogs made in the bricks are ..........
options: to reduce weight of the brick
to form a key for holding the mortar
to indicate year and name of the manufacture
to indicate top of the brick
explain: The frog is the indentation on the top face of the brick that creates a mechanical bond (key) with the mortar.

q: 35. In residential buildings the height of bathroom should not be less than ...........
explain: Under building bylaws, bathrooms usually have a minimum height requirement of 2.4 meters.

q: 36. The perpendicular distance between intrados and extrados of an arch is called
explain: The depth of an arch is defined as the perpendicular distance between its inner curve (intrados) and its outer curve (extrados).
